memory_update.text: FORM should be tracked as an HBM test-gate candidate: direct probe-card exposure to HBM wafer/stack testing, with 2026 company release citing record DRAM revenue from HBM demand.
CAMT should be tracked as an advanced-packaging inspection/metrology candidate: March 2026 OSAT orders for CoWoS-like AI packaging provide direct evidence of pull-through from AI packaging capacity.
KLIC should be tracked as a lower-attention advanced-packaging bonding-tool hypothesis: TCB/heterogeneous-integration exposure is plausible but requires updated revenue-mix verification.

AMKR is a reference OSAT anchor for this node, useful for mapping demand from 2.5D/HBM package capacity into equipment, inspection, bonding, and test suppliers rather than as the primary underfollowed target.

Later layers should verify which subsegments remain genuinely underfollowed versus already priced: HBM probe cards, CoWoS-like inspection/metrology, TCB/hybrid bonding tools, temporary bond/debond, substrate materials, interposers, thermal interface materials, and test sockets.

node: HBM and advanced-packaging inputs below the memory producers
summary: Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe around HBM and advanced-packaging inputs using an underfollowed discovery lens. The best fit for this pass is not the memory producers or AI accelerator leaders, but suppliers of inspection/metrology, probe-card test gates, thermocompression/heterogeneous-integration tools, and OSAT capacity. The list intentionally includes one reference OSAT anchor and three lower-attention equipment/test suppliers where HBM, CoWoS-like, 2.5D/3D packaging, or known-good-die testing can create second-order demand pull-through. Several links are strong enough for Layer 1 inclusion, but later layers must verify revenue mix, customer concentration, durability of orders/backlog, and whether the market has already fully discovered the exposure.
